summary.headline: IndiGo posted a Q2 FY27 net loss of INR 19 billion, though PRASK rose 31% and guidance calls for PRASK growth above 25% in Q3.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue held up, with total income of INR 243 billion (up 24% YoY) and yield up over 34%, but a 69% jump in fuel CASK and a seasonally soft quarter left a net loss of INR 19 billion (vs INR 26 billion loss a year ago). Excluding MTM and hedging, the net loss was about INR 7 billion vs a profit of about INR 1 billion last year. Management ended the widebody damp-lease operations (Norse wet lease) from 1 November, and reaffirmed FY28 mid-teens ASK growth and the long-term INR 300 billion ASKM by FY30 target. Q3 guidance: early single-digit capacity growth, load factor flat YoY, PRASK up more than 25%.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic ASKs were broadly flat YoY in Q2; management sees no need for major domestic network restructuring and will adjust capacity by area. Q3 capacity cuts are weighted to international, as the festive domestic quarter is strong.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: International ASKs fell about 2.9% YoY in Q2. Widebody damp-lease (Norse) ended 1 November; XLR used to keep Amsterdam slot; Dar es Salaam added from Mumbai from November.

segments.name: Cargo
segments.commentary: Cargo revenue grew 37% YoY in Q2; management expects strong cargo to continue in Q3, though departure of 787s will reduce long-haul cargo capacity.

segments.name: Loyalty (BluChip)
segments.commentary: Programme approaching 20 million members with more than 30 partners after two years; no bookings or revenue figures disclosed yet.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27: capacity to grow early single digits YoY; Walsh later said the Q3 ASK growth is about 3% with cuts more in international.
Q3 FY27: PRASK expected to grow more than 25% YoY, based on October trends; load factor expected flat YoY.
FY27: capacity to grow early single digits; CASK ex fuel ex forex MTM to rise high single digits to early double digits (analyst summarised as high single to low double digits, midpoint ~10%).
FY28: mid-teens ASK growth guidance unchanged, under review; A350 deliveries from 2028; more than one aircraft delivery per week expected.
Long-term ASKM target of 300 billion by FY30 reaffirmed by management; analyst estimated 18-19% CAGR needed from about 178-180 billion ASKM exit FY27.
capex_capacity: Widebody damp-lease operations concluded effective 1 November 2026, ahead of A350 arrival in 2028.
Fleet closed at 442 aircraft at quarter-end after 22 inductions (all via GIFT City entity), 10 redeliveries and 2 damp-lease returns.
No fleet review; company remains committed to Airbus orders, though some OEM delivery delays expected.
Capacity deployed on a flight-by-flight basis; Navi Mumbai airport operations being moved in, with higher charges at new airports described as long-term investment.
demand_pricing: Industry seat deployment about 5% lower YoY in Q2; IndiGo's pricing actions and capacity rationalisation supported revenue.
Management says demand has held up well; too early to call elasticity after one soft quarter.
Q3 load factor expected flat YoY on current bookings; domestic and international split not disclosed beyond the international-weighted capacity cut.
Fuel pass-through expected to continue; Walsh said fares correlate with fuel prices and expects European hedges to unwind into higher fares next year.
Jet crack spreads elevated, expected to average around 60-65% this year vs historical about 20%; crude around $110-115.
Government fuel price stabilisation fund: company will participate if terms make sense.
Premium Stretch product contribution still small in Q2, with growth expected.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the slight QoQ decline in fuel CASK?
qa_highlights.answer: The Q1 fuel cap (25% over March prices) ended 8 June, so Q2 partly benefited from a cap that was lower than market prices in April to June 8; VAT reductions also helped.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected impact of the widebody exit on spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the exit to be accretive to RASK-CASK spreads but gave no figures; international ASKs were down about 2.9% in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 capacity cuts be domestic or international?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly international, as the festive quarter is strong domestically.

qa_highlights.question: How does Q2 CASK ex-fuel guidance imply H2 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects capacity to rise in H2, so utilisation should catch up; full-year guidance was given as early double digits or late single digits (analyst reads midpoint around 10%).

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY30 300 billion ASKM target change?
qa_highlights.answer: No change; Walsh said he sees nothing that makes the long-term targets unachievable and cited unserved markets and aircraft deliveries as growth levers.

qa_highlights.question: How are premium and ancillary products performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Stretch premium product is small but encouraging; ancillary revenue per passenger rose from about INR 525 to INR 590 in Q2.

risks_watch: Jet fuel crack spreads and rupee depreciation (9% over 12 months) keep CASK elevated; management says the USD cost base is unhedged.
Load factor decline (about 2 percentage points in Q2) alongside high yields; Q3 load factor guided flat YoY.
Possible government fare-control measures and price stabilisation fund terms.
Aircraft delivery delays from OEMs could push FY28 mid-teens ASK growth; guidance under review.
Airport ownership by airports and new-airport charges (Navi Mumbai) may raise costs.
Q2 other expenses fell QoQ partly due to a reclassification of about INR 178 million (INR 178 crore) of hedging gain.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term India growth and on pricing discipline, but cautious on near-term costs; Walsh was evasive on fuel-price outlook and on loyalty and premium figures, saying it was too early to quantify them.
key_quotes: Our pricing actions and disciplined capacity deployment, together with a 5 percent reduction in industry seats, supported stronger revenue performance.
We're not going to make that mistake.
So right now, we're not changing the financial year '28 growth guidance of mid-teens.

adds.what: Widebody damp-lease (Norse) operations concluded; capacity exit, not an addition
A350 widebody deliveries from 2028 (more than one aircraft per week expected)

growth.why: Q3 FY27 capacity guided to early single-digit growth (about 3% per Walsh) and FY27 capacity cut to early single digits, with PRASK up more than 25% on October trends and flat load factor; FY28 mid-teens ASK growth is unchanged but under review and backed only by future A350 deliveries from 2028, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDAR margin rebounded to about 11% from 6% a year ago and PRASK rose 31%, but fuel CASK is up 69% YoY and FY27 CASK ex-fuel is guided up high single to early double digits (~10% midpoint), so expansion depends on fuel and fares holding.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 442 aircraft at quarter-end after 22 inductions, A350 deliveries from 2028 with more than one per week expected, and FY28 mid-teens ASK growth held but under review; OEM delays are a risk.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q3 FY27 capacity guided to early single-digit growth (about 3% per Walsh) with international cuts, and load factor down about 2 points in Q2 and guided flat YoY in Q3, so volumes grow only modestly.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is committed to Airbus orders and has no fleet review, but no new capex was guided and utilisation was not disclosed; A350 deliveries from 2028 are the main committed capacity spend.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 PRASK beat guidance at +31% vs more than 25% guided, and Q3 PRASK is guided above 25% on October trends, though fuel and CASK headwinds offset.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 capacity was cut to early single digits and CASK ex-fuel guided up high single to early double digits, FY28 mid-teens ASK growth is under review, and A350 delays are flagged, with fuel and rupee risks still open.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Premium Stretch contribution is small but growing and management expects growth; per-passenger ancillary revenue rose 12% QoQ to INR 590, though no launch dates were given.

rows.label: Fuel pass-through and fare correlation
rows.why: Walsh said fares correlate with fuel prices and European hedges are expected to unwind into higher fares next year, while jet cracks average 60-65% vs about 20% historically.

rows.label: A350 widebody deliveries from 2028
rows.why: More than one aircraft delivery per week expected from 2028, with Airbus orders firmly committed, though some OEM delivery delays are expected.

rows.label: Navi Mumbai shift and Dar es Salaam addition
rows.why: Navi Mumbai operations are being moved in with higher charges, and Dar es Salaam is added from Mumbai from November, but no capacity or revenue figures were given.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term India growth, pricing discipline and the FY30 300 billion ASKM target, but cautious on near-term fuel and CASK costs and evasive on fuel outlook, loyalty and premium figures; analysts pushed on the load factor decline, FY27 CASK guidance and the FY28 growth read
